::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 12th 1863  
**From:** Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Katherine Wykes-Sneyd
:::

My dear [Irene](people/person_538.qmd)

Many thanks for your sister’s pretty little poem. I daresay it took great effect at your tea drinking. How much more beautiful [Aytoun](people/person_1875.qmd)’s is than [Tennyson](people/person_1874.qmd)’s and what a glorious day that was![^1] I could see the bridal train rush by on the LSW, and hear the guns fired at Southampton. [Our squire](people/person_282.qmd) gave beef and beer to each family at home, and there was a grand bonfire on the hill

Thank you so much about the answers to the Sunday questions

your affectionate

Mother Goose

---

[^1]: The [Prince of Wales](people/person_1876.qmd) (later Edward VII) married Princess [Alexandra](people/person_1877.qmd) of Denmark on 10 March 1863 at St George's Chapel, Windsor. The Poet Laureate, Alfred Tennyson (1809-1892), had composed ‘A Welcome to Alexandra, March 7 1863’ beginning ‘Sea-king’s daughter from over the sea, Alexandra!’ and W.E.Aytoun (1813-1865) a ‘Nuptial Ode on the Marriage of his Royal Highness the Prince of Wales’  to celebrate the marriage.
